summary: You present a coherent preliminary reef-monitoring concept, explain why one spacecraft is proposed, and include STK evidence for orbit and access planning. To reach the next rubric level, substantiate key claims about imaging and revisit, launch compatibility, ground-station capability, sunlight conditions, and end-of-life disposal. Your conclusion and presentation also need stronger evidence-based synthesis and more consistent referencing and figure formatting.
next_steps: In Orbit, define the payload’s field of view, ground sample distance, swath, and pointing limits, then use coverage or revisit analysis to support the daily reef-imaging claim. Explain that RAAN describes orbital-plane orientation, not launch-site location, and that a sun-synchronous orbit does not guarantee continuous sunlight; support any illumination claim with the orbit design.

In Launch and Ground Control & Communications, assess Vega E’s payload and schedule compatibility for the proposed retrograde orbit. Establish that Mount Pleasant has suitable spacecraft TT&C equipment, frequencies, and operational support. State the access elevation constraint, extend the access analysis beyond a short simulation, and provide a link budget and data-rate basis for concluding that contact is sufficient.

In Mission Duration & EOL, reconcile the stated lack of thrusters with the proposed passive drag sail by sizing the sail and estimating decay time against an acceptable disposal period. Then strengthen the Conclusion by drawing only evidence-supported findings and limitations. For presentation, number and title figures and tables consistently, complete and cross-check citations, and replace Wikipedia with an appropriate source.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction explains the reef-monitoring purpose and environmental rationale, justifies using one spacecraft, and identifies likely science and government customers. To reach Accomplished, name the spacecraft operator explicitly, clarify the roles of operators and customers, and support the rationale with appropriate literature.
criteria.C2: In Launch, Orbit, Ground Control & Communications, and Mission Duration & EOL, you address the major design elements and include STK access evidence (Images 1–5). To reach Accomplished, substantiate launch compatibility, imaging and revisit, station TT&C capability, link performance, and drag-sail decay time. Correct the RAAN and sunlight explanations and support access conclusions quantitatively.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion recaps the main design choices and notes uncertainty about the launch vehicle. To reach Accomplished, draw detailed conclusions from demonstrated evidence and acknowledge limitations: in particular, qualify the claims about consistent illumination and Mount Pleasant access using verified orbit, coverage, and ground-station results.
criteria.C4: Your report has a recognizable engineering structure, an executive summary, and useful figures and data. To reach Accomplished, make figure and table numbering and titles consistent, improve writing and formatting consistency, and ensure every in-text citation matches a complete reference-list entry. Replace the cited Wikipedia source with an appropriate reference.
